To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the purification of the hemicellulose extract by ultrafiltration and ion exchange chromatography followed by spray drying is an efficient way of producing a high purity hemicellulotic polymer, and (b) this approach allows to determine the optimal conditions of the ultrafiltrations step.

The technical performances of purification process based on ultrafiltration and anion exchange chromatographies are less attractive than those of the ethanol precipitation but with a lower consumption of energy and ethanol.
the technical and environmental performance of extraction and purification of hemicellulose from wheat straw and wheat bran were evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an environmentally friendly process for the extraction of hemicellulose from wheat straw and/or bran.
the development of an environment-friendly process for hemiceluloses extraction and purification.
the development of a new environment-friendly process for arabinoxylans extraction and purification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a purification process based on ultrafiltration, ion-exchange and spray drying is the most appropriate for the extraction of hemicellulose from wheat straw and wheat bran.
the technical and environmental considerations have shown that the purification of arabinoxylan extracts by UF-CHR-SD is a promising alternative to the purification process based on EV-P-FD.
the technical performance of the second process (with a lower energetic and water consumption) is less attractive but with an acceptable environmental impact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the technical performances of the first purification step (EV/P/FD) are better than the second one (UF/CHR/SD) but with a higher environmental impacts.
the technical and environmental aspects of the studied purification process are compatible with the production of arabinoxylan powder for industrial applications.

purification by ultrafiltration and anion exchange chromatographic purification are more attractive than the evaporation/ethanol precipitation/freezing drying process from an environmental point of view.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the technical and environmental considerations should be coupled in order to develop a process that is both technically and environmentally efficient.

the purification step is a critical step in the process of arabinoxylan extraction from straw and bran, and that the choice of the purification step is crucial to reduce the environmental impact of the whole process.
the combination of technical and environmental performances is a useful tool to optimize the extraction and purification processes.
